item.title: Monte Carlo Dropout for Object Detection on Point Clouds
item.description: In this work, we take VoteNet, a state-of-the-art deep neural network for object detection, as a basis and extend it for computing epistemic uncertainty in itspredictions with Monte Carlo dropout. We show that this quantity can be used as a weighting factor for predictions, leading to an increase in the overall performance ofthe model, and also as a metric for selecting the most beneficial scenes to annotate for training from unknown data for active learning scenarios.

item.title: Indirect Visual Odometry With Optical Flow
item.description:
Extending a Stereo camera Visual Odometry implementation with Optical Flow per the paper by Usenko et al. Optical flow was used to track detected Keypoints through frames and again was used to carry them to the other camera to triangulate 3D points in the map.

  • Initial implementation of a stereo Visual Odometry application from a provided template.
  • Adopting an Optical Flow approach to track key points through frames.
  • Using Optical Flow to move key points from one camera to the other.
  • Using the key points matched from both cameras to triangulate 3D points for mapping.

item.title: Analysis and Experiments on Deep Closest Points Architecture
item.description: The goal of the project was to conduct experiments and analyze their results on the DCP architecture by Wang et al. Mixamo dataset was used to retrain the model and some tests were also done with the TUM RGBD dataset. Tried adding different regularizations, adding color as an additional input signal, and different sampling of points to improve the performance of the model in real-life scenarios.

item.title: 3D Real-Time Instance Segmentation with LDLS-YOLACT
item.description:
In this project I’ve developed a 3D object detection and tracking pipeline for autonomous driving with Python and ROS without any labeled 3D data. Our hardware were only a Livox mid-100 lidar sensor and a RealSense camera. After calibrating the sensors, the pipeline is as follows:

  • Get 2D instance segmentation of the current camera image using YOLACT.
  • Update the id numbers of the detected entitites using SORT
  • Project the masks into 3D point cloud using LDLS
  • Compute the 3D bounding boxes for the detected areas.

Source code can be found here page. For the implementation with ROS, please get in touch.

item.title: KinectFusion: Dense Surface Mapping and Tracking
item.description: Implementation of the paper KinectFusion by Microsoft using C++ and CUDA. The goal of the project is to develop a method for accurate real-time mapping of indoor scenes, using only a low-cost depth camera and graphics hardware. Presentation video can be seen below.

item.title: Multiple Object Tracking with Tracktor++
item.description: Implemented vanilla Tracktor with Faster-RCNN using PyTorch. Added a basic motion model and also a reidentificaiton network as the paper suggested for Tracktor++.

item.title: Divergence-Free Shape Correspondence with Time Dependent Vector Fields
item.description: We extended the paper “Divergence-Free Shape Correspondence by Deformation” and representing a motion sequence as a time dependent vector field. We solve correspondence and matching problems for the whole sequence during the optimization. Some of the current results can be seen below. Blue is shape is our estimated deformation and orange is the ground truth in the Dynamic FAUST dataset.

item.title: Plant Disease Classification
item.description: Detection of plant diseases via computer vision based systems are being used to identify plant diseases promptly, to prevent the spread of the disease. In this work, we present a system for classifying plant diseases from photographs of the diseased parts of the plant. The system is trained using transfer learning on convolutional neural networks (VGGNet) which are trained to classify 38 plant diseases or 11 disease classes. 95.09% average accuracy was obtained on plant-disease classification using PlantVillage dataset. On the other hand, 96.27% average accuracy was obtained for disease classification instead of plant-disease classification. VGGNet obtained these scores.

item.title: One Table to Count Them All: Parallel Frequency Estimation on Single-Board Computers
item.description:
Abstract: Sketches are probabilistic data structures that can provide approximate results within mathematically proven error bounds while using orders of magnitude less memory than traditional approaches. They are tailored for streaming data analysis on architectures even with limited memory such as single-board computers that are widely exploited for IoT and edge computing. Since these devices offer multiple cores, with efficient parallel sketching schemes, they are able to manage high volumes of data streams. However, since their caches are relatively small, a careful parallelization is required. In this work, we focus on the frequency estimation problem and evaluate the performance of a high-end server, a 4-core Raspberry Pi and an 8-core Odroid. As a sketch, we employed the widely used Count-Min Sketch. To hash the stream in parallel and in a cache-friendly way, we applied a novel tabulation approach and rearranged the auxiliary tables into a single one. To parallelize the process with performance, we modified the workflow and applied a form of buffering between hash computations and sketch updates. Today, many single-board computers have heterogeneous processors in which slow and fast cores are equipped together. To utilize all these cores to their full potential, we proposed a dynamic load-balancing mechanism which significantly increased the performance of frequency estimation.
